key_insight: The paper demonstrates direct-write, site-selective fabrication of individual perovskite quantum dots with near-atomic spatial control, enabling deterministic single-photon emitters.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to integrate colloidal quantum emitters with photonic devices on demand, overcoming the randomness that has limited scalable quantum photonic manufacturing.
method: Thermal scanning probe creates a nanoscale-confined reaction volume.
Perovskite QDs are synthesized directly at chosen sites with <25 nm placement control.
Emitter locations are matched to photonic cavities for deterministic coupling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-yield arrays of CsPbI3 single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths, up to 98% single-photon purity at room temperature, and enhanced spontaneous emission when coupled to cavities.
watch_item: The approach still relies on precise nanoscale thermal scanning and material control, which may pose challenges for throughput, reproducibility, and device-scale integration.
paper_title: Direct writing of individual quantum dots
